title: First African Digital Humanism Summer School 2025

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating multimodal LLM outputs (text and images) against norm-compliant and norm-violating prompts based on traditional greeting practices across five distinct societies (Baganda, Luo, Hausa, Chinese, Brazilian), utilizing human-in-the-loop review by native experts to measure cultural fidelity, spatial behavior, and etiquette.

Comparing the accuracy, intelligibility, and translation quality of LLMs and language detection tools on underrepresented African languages (e.g., Yoruba, Kinyarwanda, Amharic, Swahili, Kikuyu) versus English, using clean news text, code-switched social media data, and official administrative documents.

Analyzing AI-generated visual and textual outputs for gender protocol violations in cultural contexts (e.g., misgendering characters, violating female hair-covering norms in Hausa greetings) and testing LLMs with employment-related queries in various African languages to detect biased associations.

Evaluating LLM-generated thematic summaries of public policy consultations to determine if minority, highly technical, or non-English stakeholder viewpoints are systematically underrepresented or diluted compared to widely expressed majority perspectives.
